Event Clocks from two venues: separating common news from venue noise

Source: R/measure.R
event_clock_venues.Rd

When the same event trades on two venues (say Polymarket and Kalshi), each venue's measured clock contains the common information flow plus venue-specific noise (bid-ask bounce, stale quotes, idiosyncratic flows). Comparing four clocks built from synchronized prices separates the two:

A_x, A_y

each venue's own clock, \(\sum (\Delta L)^2\).

A_composite

the clock of the equal-weight average of the two venues' log odds.

A_cross

the cross-venue clock \(\sum \Delta L^x \Delta L^y\): news moves both venues, so it survives the product; independent venue noise does not, so on average it drops out.

Usage

event_clock_venues(x, y, from = NULL, to = NULL, labels = NULL, clip = NULL)

Arguments

x, y

event_prices objects (or coercible) for the same event outcome on two venues.

from

Valuation date/time (default: first observation).

to

One or more horizon dates/times (default: last observation = full sample). Names are used as horizon labels.

labels

Optional venue labels (default: the market_ids).

clip

Numeric length-2 clipping bounds for q before the log-odds transform; defaults to the bounds stored in x.

Value

A tibble with one row per horizon: venue_x, venue_y, from, to, horizon, n_common (synchronized observations), A_x, A_y, A_composite, A_cross, corr (correlation of the two venues' log-odds changes), noise_share_x, noise_share_y.

Details

Under a simple benchmark in which each venue's log odds are the common latent log odds plus independent noise, \(E[A_x] = A + N_x\) while \(E[A_{cross}] = A\). The reported noise_share_x \(= 1 - A_{cross}/A_x\) is then the fraction of venue x's measured clock attributable to its own noise. In finite samples A_cross can fall below zero when there is little common news; it is a diagnostic, not an exact measurement. The identity \(A_{composite} = (A_x + A_y + 2A_{cross})/4\) holds exactly.

Multiple venues help diagnose timing and filter venue-specific noise, but they cannot by themselves pin down the absolute physical clock scale; that still rests on the recovery restriction (see ec_recovery_set()).

Prices are matched on identical timestamps. Synchronize intraday series first, e.g. with a common daily snapshot: pm_daily(x, snapshot_hour = 15.75) takes the last price at or before 15:45 New York time.

References

Hanke, Schadner, Stöckl, and Weissensteiner (Working Paper), "The Event Clock: What State Prices Identify About Physical Information".

See also

event_clock_venues_path() for the cumulative clocks.

Examples

# two noisy venues observing the same simulated news
set.seed(7)
p <- ec_simulate_path(1, 120, q = 0.5, A = 1)
days <- as.Date("2024-06-01") + 0:120
noisy <- function(sd) data.frame(time = days,
  q = ec_ilogit(p$L + stats::rnorm(121, sd = sd)))
event_clock_venues(noisy(0.05), noisy(0.10), labels = c("A", "B"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 13
#>   venue_x venue_y from       to         horizon n_common   A_x   A_y A_composite
#>   <chr>   <chr>   <date>     <date>     <chr>      <int> <dbl> <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 A       B       2024-06-01 2024-09-29 2024-0…      121  1.32  2.94        1.50
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: A_cross <dbl>, corr <dbl>, noise_share_x <dbl>,
#> #   noise_share_y <dbl>
